en.name: Grits, boxed
en.summary: A box of dry grits keeps 12 months from purchase in a cool, dry cupboard. The dry product is stable; cooked grits are a different food altogether, and a pot of them left to cool slowly on the stove is one of the classic starchy-food hazards.
en.pantry: Cool, dry and dark, 12 months from the date you bought it. Dry milled corn keeps well because there is almost no water in it, so what shortens the life is damp, warmth and insects rather than bacteria — a cardboard box is not an airtight container, so once the inner bag is open, decant into a sealed jar or clip the bag hard. Stone-ground grits still carry the germ and its oil and will go rancid sooner than degerminated quick grits; if you buy them, buy small and use them faster.
en.fridge: Dry grits do not need refrigeration and the cupboard is the drier place, so keep them there unless you have bought stone-ground grits in a hot kitchen, in which case cold slows the oil in the germ down. Either way, seal the jar hard first — the fridge is humid and the meal will cake. Cooked grits are an entirely separate matter: they are a wet cooked starch, and they belong in a shallow covered container in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, not left warm in the saucepan.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for dry boxed grits, and a dry good with a year in the cupboard has little to gain from it. Freezing is genuinely useful for one purpose: killing any weevil eggs in a bulk buy before you store it. If you do that, seal the bag airtight and let it return to room temperature before opening, so condensation lands on the bag and not on the meal.
spoilage: A stale or rancid, oily smell — most likely in stone-ground grits.
Weevils, moths, webbing or fine dust in the bag.
Clumping or caking from absorbed moisture.
Musty smell or visible mould in a bag that got damp.
tips: Decant the opened bag into an airtight jar; the box is not a seal.
Buy stone-ground grits in small quantities — the germ makes them go rancid faster.
Label the jar with the purchase date.
Cool cooked grits quickly in a shallow container and refrigerate; do not leave the pot on the stove.

faq.q: How long do boxed grits last?
faq.a: 12 months from purchase in a cool, dry cupboard, sealed against damp and insects.

faq.q: Do grits need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: Dry grits do not. Stone-ground grits benefit from cold in a hot kitchen because of the oil in the germ. Cooked grits always need the fridge.

faq.q: How can you tell if grits have gone bad?
faq.a: A rancid or musty smell, caking, or any sign of insects. Dry grits that smell clean and pour freely are fine.

zh.name: 玉米粗粉（盒裝）
zh.summary: 盒裝的乾玉米粗粉從購買日起算，放陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃可放 12 個月。乾的很穩定；煮熟之後則完全是另一種食物，一鍋慢慢放涼的玉米糊，正是澱粉類食品最典型的風險場景。
zh.pantry: 陰涼、乾燥、避光，自購買日起 12 個月。乾燥的玉米製品幾乎不含水，所以縮短它壽命的是潮濕、高溫和蟲，而不是細菌。紙盒不是密封容器，內袋一開就請倒進密封罐，或把袋口確實夾緊。石磨（保留胚芽）的玉米粗粉含油，比去胚芽的快煮款更早走油；如果買的是石磨款，就少量買、快點用完。
zh.fridge: 乾的玉米粗粉不需要冷藏，櫥櫃本來就比較乾，除非你在濕熱的廚房裡買了石磨款，低溫才有意義，因為它能壓住胚芽裡的油脂。不管怎樣，罐子都要先密封好，冰箱是潮濕的，粉會結塊。煮好的玉米糊則完全是另一回事：那是含水的熟澱粉，要裝在淺的加蓋容器裡放 4 °C 以下冷藏，而不是溫溫地留在鍋子裡。
zh.freezer: 乾玉米粗粉沒有公布的冷凍期限，一個能在櫥櫃放一年的乾貨，從冷凍得到的好處也有限。冷凍真正有用的只有一件事：大量採買時先冷凍幾天，把可能存在的蟲卵處理掉。這麼做的話請確實密封，並等整包回到室溫再拆開，讓水氣凝在袋子上而不是粉上。
spoilage: 有陳味或油耗味，石磨款最常見。
出現米蟲、蛾、絲網或袋底細粉。
受潮的袋子出現霉味或看得到霉。
tips: 開封後倒進密封罐，紙盒本身不算密封。
石磨款少量買，有胚芽就比較快走油。
煮好的玉米糊要用淺容器快速降溫再冷藏，不要把鍋子留在爐上。

faq.q: 盒裝玉米粗粉可以放多久？
faq.a: 自購買日起，密封防潮防蟲放陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃 12 個月。
乾的不用。石磨款在濕熱廚房冷藏有幫助，因為胚芽含油。煮熟的則一定要冷藏。

faq.q: 怎麼知道玉米粗粉壞了？
faq.a: 有油耗味或霉味、結塊，或看到蟲。乾爽、聞起來乾淨、倒得出來的就沒問題。
